lessons.title: Flexi Benefit Plans: Choosing Your Components Each Year

children.text: Every April, a payroll portal at companies like yours sends the same email: "Flexi Benefit Plan declaration window is now open. Please allocate your FBP amount of ₹2,40,000 by 30 April." Most people click "Allocate all to special allowance" and move on.

That click is a decision. It usually means paying more tax than necessary, and it locks you out of some benefits until next April. This lesson shows how a flexi plan works, what to pick under each regime, and the calendar habits that stop a surprise TDS spike in March.

body.text: A flexi plan does not create tax savings. It lets you claim the ones the law already allows, if you choose them in time and back them with bills.

children.text: How a flexi benefit plan works
is a slice of your CTC that you allocate across a menu of components. The rules differ between companies, but most plans share the same mechanics:

markDefs.definition: A portion of CTC that the employee can allocate each year across a menu of components such as meal vouchers, phone reimbursement, fuel, LTA and books. Any amount not allocated or not claimed is usually paid as taxable special allowance.

children.text: A fixed annual FBP amount inside CTC, often shown as "Flexi Pay" or "Benefits Basket"
A declaration window at the start of the year, and sometimes one more mid-year
Some components paid monthly as vouchers or cards (meal cards, gift cards)
Others paid only when you submit bills (phone, fuel, books, LTA)
Anything you do not allocate, or allocate but never claim, is usually paid as fully taxable special allowance, often at year-end
A proof submission deadline, typically between December and February

events.title: Declare your tax regime and FBP allocation
events.description: Tell your employer whether you are in the old or new regime, and allocate your basket. In the old regime, also declare rent and investments in Form 124.

events.title: Use vouchers and upload bills
events.description: Meal and gift cards are loaded. Upload phone, fuel and other bills monthly so claims are processed with salary.

events.title: Proof deadline
events.description: Final date for bills and old regime proofs. Unsubstantiated claims are treated as taxable, and TDS is recalculated.

events.title: Year-end settlement
events.description: Unclaimed amounts are paid out as taxable salary, and any TDS shortfall is recovered from the last salaries.

events.title: File your return
events.description: Salaried employees without business income can choose either regime in their return, even if they declared differently to their employer.

body.title: The LTA default
body.question: Ritika is in the new regime. Her flexi plan put ₹40,000 into LTA by default last year, and she never claimed it. What happened for tax?
options: The ₹40,000 was tax-free because it was allocated to LTA
The ₹40,000 was paid as taxable salary, exactly as if it were special allowance
She can claim the exemption when filing her return
body.explanation: In the new regime, LTA is fully taxable whether claimed or not. Most plans pay unclaimed amounts as taxable salary at year-end, so she did not lose money, but the allocation gave her no tax benefit. That ₹40,000 would have been better placed in meal vouchers, phone or fuel.

children.text: Ritika, an analytics manager in Hyderabad, has an FBP amount of ₹2,40,000. She is in the new regime and her taxable income is about ₹17,00,000 after her claims, so her top slab is 20%. She eats lunch at office, drives a 1.2 litre car for client visits and personal errands, and has a ₹1,500 monthly phone and broadband bill.

data.label: Fuel and car running (₹5,000 a month)

stats.label: Tax if all taken as special allowance
Saved
stats.context: Per year, with the same CTC

body.title: Check Ritika's saving
body.prompt: Ritika's tax is ₹1,45,600 on taxable income of ₹17,00,000. Without her ₹1,45,800 of flexi claims, taxable income would be ₹18,45,800. Calculate the tax at that income under the new regime, including 4% cess and rounding to the nearest ₹10, then find how much she saves.

children.text: Varun, a project manager in Chennai, has the same ₹2,40,000 FBP amount but is in the old regime and in the 30% slab. He has two school-going children, takes one domestic family trip a year, and buys technical books and journals for work.

columns.label: Ritika, new regime
points: No LTA, education or books: taxable anyway

body.text: Varun still has ₹30,200 left in his basket. If he uses his car for work, fuel reimbursement could absorb most of it. The old regime has more tax-free components on the menu, which is exactly why a thoughtless "all to special allowance" choice costs old regime employees more.

children.text: Your employer calculates TDS assuming your declared claims will be backed by bills. If you do not upload bills by the proof deadline, those claims are treated as taxable, and the entire shortfall in TDS is recovered from your last few salaries.

body.title: Ritika's monthly TDS: bills on time vs bills missed until January

series.label: Claims disallowed at the January deadline

body.label: Extra TDS per month in January to March if Ritika misses her proof deadline
body.context: Her tax rises by ₹30,330 for the year, and about ₹1,09,200 has already been deducted by December, so ₹66,730 must be recovered from three salaries: about ₹22,243 a month instead of ₹12,133.

body.text: If you declared the old regime to your employer and miss proofs, you can still claim genuine exemptions and deductions when filing your return and get a refund. But flexi reimbursements like phone and fuel generally depend on your employer processing bills, so a missed deadline usually means that benefit is simply lost for the year.

body.title: Pro-rata basket
body.prompt: Zoya joins on 1 October with an annual FBP amount of ₹1,80,000 that is pro-rated for the months worked. How much can she allocate for her first tax year?
body.explanation: October to March is 6 months: ₹1,80,000 × 6 ÷ 12 = ₹90,000. Her maximum tax-free meal card for those months at ₹200 per meal for 22 working days is ₹26,400, so she should size components to her shorter year.

body.title: Old regime only
body.textWithBlank: For parents in the old regime, the flexi component worth up to ₹3,000 a month per child is the children ___ allowance.
body.explanation: Children education allowance is exempt up to ₹3,000 a month per child, for a maximum of 2 children, under the Income-tax Rules, 2026. It is fully taxable in the new regime.

body.title: Ritika considers switching regimes
body.scenario: In April, Ritika declared the new regime and built her basket around it. In September she starts paying ₹45,000 a month rent after moving to a bigger flat in Gachibowli, and her colleague says she should "switch to the old regime and put everything into LTA and HRA". Her flexi plan allows one mid-year change in October.
body.prompt: What should Ritika consider before changing her regime or flexi allocation mid-year?
body.modelAnswer: First, the regime question does not have to be settled with the employer mid-year: as a salaried employee without business income, she can choose either regime when filing her return. The employer declaration mainly decides how TDS is deducted. Second, she should run both regimes on her full-year numbers: HRA exemption only for the months she pays rent, her actual investments under Section 123 and health insurance under Section 126, versus the new regime with its ₹75,000 standard deduction and lower slabs. Third, the flexi choices that matter in both regimes (meal card, phone, fuel, gifts) should stay as they are. LTA helps only in the old regime and only if she actually takes a domestic trip and has tickets. If the old regime clearly wins, she can use the October window to add LTA and declare rent to her employer so TDS falls. If it is close, she can keep the new regime at work, keep documents, and decide when filing.

body.title: Your annual flexi plan routine
steps: April: estimate your tax under both regimes before declaring
April: allocate your basket to components that work in your regime, sized to real spending
Monthly: upload phone, fuel and other bills with each salary cycle
Mid-year: revisit if rent, family or car situation has changed
Before the proof deadline: check every declared claim has a matching bill or proof
March: review your final payslip and Form 16 for unclaimed amounts taxed as salary
At filing: choose the regime that gives you lower tax on your actual numbers

body.text: Flexi plan rules, deadlines and payout of unclaimed amounts vary between employers. Figures use tax year 2026-27 rules. The car running cost treatment follows the approach explained earlier in this course. This lesson is for education and is not personalised tax advice.

points: A flexi plan lets you allocate part of CTC to components the tax law already favours. Unallocated or unclaimed amounts are taxed as salary.
In the new regime, prioritise meal cards, phone and internet, fuel for work use and gift vouchers. Skip LTA, education allowance and books.
In the old regime, add children education and hostel allowances, LTA and books where they match real spending.
On a ₹2,40,000 basket, sensible choices saved Ritika ₹30,330 in the new regime and Varun about ₹65,458 in the old regime.
Missing the proof deadline can push your TDS up sharply in the last months of the year.
Salaried employees can choose their regime when filing the return, whatever they declared to the employer.
